card.stem: The sketch shows a tiled roof of a dwelling house, which is supported on a 350 mm external concrete block wall with an insulated cavity. The roof is a traditional cut roof and has a pitch of 45°.
card.questionText: To a scale of 1:5, draw a vertical section through the eaves of the tiled roof and the external wall. Show the typical construction details from a level 400 mm below the wall plate, through the eaves and include three courses of tiles at eaves. Include the roof insulation and show clearly the ventilation path to the roof structure at the eaves. Include three typical dimensions.

rows.verbatim: Any 7 of the above details (5 marks each)
rows.contextNote: Credit the best SEVEN acceptable details at 5 marks each, capped at 35. Marked details: concrete tiles; 44 × 35 mm battens; breathable membrane; rafters 150–250 × 40 mm; roof insulation; 150 × 40 mm ceiling joists; 12.5 mm foil-backed plasterboard and skim; 100 × 75 mm wallplate; internal plaster and external render; 100 mm inner leaf; wall insulation; 50 mm residual cavity; 100 mm outer leaf; fascia and soffit; 100 mm eaves gutter; ventilation path.
Three typical dimensions on the section.

card.stem: A dwelling house, as shown in the sketch, has a 300 mm external block wall with 50 mm expanded polystyrene insulation in the cavity. The wall has a smooth external render finish. It is proposed to improve the insulation properties of the wall by adding an external system of insulation.
card.questionText: Using notes and neat freehand sketches, show one suitable method of applying an external insulation system to the wall. Specify the insulation material used, indicate its typical thickness and include details of the external surface finish to the insulation.

rows.contextNote: Such as: slabs of insulation fixed to the wall with adhesive and mechanical fixings.
A second, different step. Such as: an acrylic basecoat with a fibre mesh embedded for impact resistance; a coloured primer.

rows.verbatim: Details of external surface finish to the insulation
rows.contextNote: Such as: a coloured, textured acrylic render, trowelled or sprayed, durable and in a range of colours.

rows.verbatim: Type and thickness of insulation (3 marks + 3marks)
rows.contextNote: Type 3 and thickness 3. Such as: expanded polystyrene, at least 120 mm and up to 300 mm; phenolic foam, at least 75 mm; or Gutex or cork.
Two valid details on the sketch, 4 each, and the quality of the sketch, excellent 8, good 6, fair 4.

card.stem: A dwelling house, as shown in the sketch, has a 300 mm external block wall with 50 mm expanded polystyrene insulation in the cavity. The wall has a smooth external render finish. It is proposed to improve the insulation properties of the wall by adding an external system of insulation.

card.stem: A strip foundation is designed to support a 350 mm external wall of a dwelling house. The wall is of concrete block construction with an insulated cavity, as shown in the sketch.
card.questionText: Describe, using notes and neat freehand sketches, the design of a typical strip foundation for the above external wall under the following headings: width and depth of trench; finished level of concrete in foundation; reinforcement of foundation; position of wall on strip foundation.

rows.contextNote: Primary communication 6 and other communication 4. Such as: at least three times the wall thickness, 1050 mm for a 350 mm wall; as deep as the ground needs, at least 600 mm to the top of the concrete, below the frost line.

rows.verbatim: Finish level of concrete in foundation
rows.contextNote: Primary communication 6 and other communication 4. Such as: pegs driven into the trench base, projecting by the foundation thickness, levelled with a straight edge and laser level.

Primary communication 6 and other communication 4. Such as: ribbed mild steel bars supported 75 mm from the bottom, where the tension is; concrete poured, vibrated and compacted around them; or steel mesh.

rows.verbatim: Position of wall on strip foundation
rows.contextNote: Primary communication 6 and other communication 4. Such as: the wall central on the foundation, with equal projections on both sides.

card.questionText: Discuss two environmental reasons why a strip foundation is the preferred foundation type for the external wall of the house.

card.questionText: List two specific safety precautions that should be observed in each of the following situations and give one reason for each safety precaution listed: manually lifting a load from a floor; placing concrete in a foundation trench from a ready-mix truck.

rows.verbatim: Safety precautions when lifting a load
rows.contextNote: Two precautions 4 each and reasons 2. Such as: stand close, back straight, bend the knees; test the load and get help if too heavy; keep it close to the body; do not twist; a clear, tidy area — protecting your back.

rows.verbatim: Safety precautions when placing concrete in a foundation
rows.contextNote: Two precautions 4 each and reasons 2. Such as: a high visibility jacket, boots and helmet; the driver able to see the work; the truck kept back from the trench edge in wet weather; a deep trench supported; only qualified workers with Safe Pass.

card.questionText: Explain, with the aid of notes and neat freehand sketches, any five of the following: rainwater butt; box dovetail joint; compression joint; wall tie; gully trap; angle bead; newel post; through and through sawing; biscuit joint.

rows.contextNote: Explain any five of the nine terms. Each term is marked separately: primary communication of relevant information 6 and other communication 4, in notes or sketches (the scheme reserves no fixed split between them). Rainwater butt: a barrel or tank connected to the downpipe to collect rainwater from the roof, with an overflow and a tap at the base; 100–300 litres; part of rainwater harvesting. Box Dovetail Joint: a joint for box shapes and drawers in quality furniture, by hand or machine; slope 1:6 for softwood, 1:8 for hardwood; decorative, with contrasting woods. Compression joint: a brass or PVC plumbing joint for copper or PVC pipe: the ends cut square, the nut and olive slipped on, and the nut tightened to compress the olive into a watertight joint. Wall tie: a stainless steel fitting holding the two leaves of a cavity wall together so they act as one, and holding the insulation; at 900 mm horizontally and 450 mm vertically. Gully trap: a PVC fitting at the head of an underground drain collecting waste or rainwater, with a grid against leaves and a water seal keeping odours and gases in the drain; it may have a back inlet. Angle bead: a stainless, galvanised steel or plastic bead with a solid rib and mesh flanges, fixed with nails or plaster dabs to give a true, reinforced plaster corner inside or out. Newel Post: a hardwood or softwood post, usually 75 × 75 or 100 × 100 mm, at the top or bottom of the stairs string or at a landing, supporting the handrail; square or round, often shaped or carved. Through and through sawing: plain sawing: the log cut straight through into boards, with little waste and the widest boards, but boards likely to cup in seasoning and no particular grain pattern. Biscuit joint: a biscuit joiner cuts crescent grooves in the edges for compressed beech biscuits, glued and cramped; ideal for joining boards edge to edge.
